root: Contract of guarantee — three parties, three contracts
rootSub: s. 126: to perform the promise, or discharge the liability, of a third person in case of his default

children.title: 1. Creditor ↔ Principal debtor
bullets: The main contract (loan, credit sale, employment)
Its existence is the basis of the guarantee

children.title: 2. Creditor ↔ Surety
bullets: Surety promises to pay / perform on default

children.title: 3. Principal debtor ↔ Surety
bullets: Surety recovers what he rightfully paid

cards.title: Revocation
cards.text: Continuing guarantee — by notice or by the surety's death, as to future transactions (ss. 130–131)

cards.title: Variance
cards.text: Any change in terms without the surety's consent — as to later transactions (s. 133)

cards.title: Release of debtor
cards.text: Contract releasing the debtor, or creditor's act / omission discharging him (s. 134)

cards.title: Composition / time / not to sue
cards.text: Binding promise with the debtor (s. 135) — not with a third person (s. 136), not mere forbearance (s. 137)

cards.title: Impairing surety's remedy
cards.text: Creditor's act or omission inconsistent with the surety's rights (s. 139)

cards.title: Loss of securities
cards.text: To the extent of the value of the security lost or parted with (s. 141)

cards.title: Not discharged
cards.text: Release of a co-surety (s. 138); debtor's discharge by operation of law

cards.title: Performance
cards.text: Payment by the debtor or the surety ends the guarantee

children.title: Express
children.text: Words spoken or written — power of attorney (s. 187)

children.title: Implied
children.text: From circumstances / course of dealing (s. 187 — Quetta shop); incidental (s. 188)

children.title: Estoppel
children.text: Principal's words or conduct induce belief in authority (s. 237)

children.title: Necessity
children.text: Emergency; cannot contact principal; prudent act (s. 189; Swaffield)

children.title: Ratification
children.text: Act on behalf of an existing principal adopted with full knowledge (ss. 196–200)

children.title: Operation of law
children.text: E.g., partners as agents of the firm (Partnership Act); legal representatives

cards.title: AGREEMENT TO SELL — later / on condition

root: Implied conditions and warranties — Sale of Goods Act
rootSub: may be excluded by agreement, dealing or usage (s. 62)

children.title: Disclosure — s. 16A
bullets: Seller must inform buyer of defects

children.title: Caveat emptor
bullets: General rule in s. 16 opening words

q.ask: Are the goods unascertained or future?
q.yes: No property until ascertained (s. 18); then on unconditional appropriation with assent, or delivery to carrier (s. 23)
q.no: Specific / ascertained — property passes when intended (s. 19); go on

q.ask: Unconditional contract, goods in a deliverable state?
q.yes: Property passes when the contract is made (s. 20)

q.ask: Must the seller do something to make them deliverable?
q.yes: Passes when done and buyer has notice (s. 21)

q.ask: Must the seller weigh / measure / test to fix the price?
q.yes: Passes when done and buyer has notice (s. 22)

q.ask: Sent on approval or sale or return?
q.yes: On approval / adopting act, or after fixed / reasonable time (s. 24)
q.no: Check reservation of right of disposal (s. 25)

root: Nemo dat quod non habet — s. 27
rootSub: a buyer from a non-owner gets no better title — except:

children.title: Estoppel
children.text: Owner's conduct precludes denial of authority (s. 27)

children.title: Mercantile agent
children.text: Possession with owner's consent; ordinary course; good faith (s. 27 proviso)

children.title: Voidable title
children.text: Contract under s. 19 / 19A not yet rescinded (s. 29)

children.title: Seller in possession
children.text: Delivery to a second buyer in good faith (s. 30(1))

children.title: Buyer in possession
children.text: Possession with seller's consent; defeats seller's lien (s. 30(2))

children.title: Other laws
children.text: Finder (s. 169), pawnee (s. 176), unpaid seller resale (s. 54(3)), court sales

children.title: No market overt
children.text: Open-market sales give no special title in Pakistan

rootSub: anything agreed, or that puts the goods in the buyer's possession (s. 33)

children.title: Actual
children.text: Physical handing over of the goods to the buyer or his agent

children.title: Symbolic
children.text: Keys of the godown; bill of lading; railway receipt; car documents and keys

children.title: Constructive (attornment)
children.text: Person in possession acknowledges he holds for the buyer (s. 36(3))

root.title: Unpaid seller
root.sub: price not wholly paid or tendered; instrument dishonoured (s. 45)
